title: Evolution by Natural Selection
text: Evolution is the change in the heritable characteristics of biological populations over successive generations. Charles Darwin and Alfred Russel Wallace independently proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection in the 19th century. Natural selection is the process whereby organisms with favorable traits that improve survival and reproduction tend to leave more offspring, causing those traits to become more common in subsequent generations. Genetic variation, which provides the raw material for natural selection, arises through mutations and recombination. Over millions of years, this process has led to the diversity of life on Earth, from single-celled bacteria to complex multicellular organisms including humans.
